note: The rules that legitimately keep --text-tertiary. THIS FILE IS HAND-AUTHORED AND HAS NO GENERATOR. No script writes it; no command regenerates it; every entry is a reviewed human decision in a PR diff. That absence is the whole guarantee — a comparison set that can be mechanically regenerated from the thing being checked cannot red, and this repo has shipped three vacuous gates already. If contrast-guard.test.js goes red, the fix is to change the CSS or to argue for a new entry here in review; it is never to regenerate this file, because there is nothing to run. Measurements justifying each entry live in contrast-audit.json, which the guard never reads (D64, plan 5c).

reasonValues.size>=24px: computed size clears the WCAG large-text threshold (24px, or 18.66px bold). KEPT only. ZERO members today, which is correct rather than suspicious: the largest computed size anywhere in the 75-key population is 19.2px.
reasonValues.decorative: genuinely decorative content that carries no information. KEPT only.
reasonValues.inactive-control: the WCAG SC 1.4.3 exemption for inactive user-interface components. KEPT only.
reasonValues.non-text: not text at all — an SVG stroke that paints no glyph. NON_TEXT only. These fall under SC 1.4.11, or are exempt outright as decorative graphics with a text alternative, and a text bar is a category error on them. Carried as issue #76; NOT to be resolved by moving them to --text-secondary, which would remove the evidence of the violation without fixing it.
reasonValues.ladder-step: the rule is a third-step site of the type ladder and must KEEP --text-tertiary. RESTORED only. #66 substituted --text-secondary here because --text-tertiary was --warm-400 against both themes and failed 4.5:1 on three of four grounds; #75 repointed it per theme (--warm-350 dark, --warm-450 light) and Andrew's ruling restored these rules. They are on this list so the guard reds if one of them stops declaring the token again -- the `missing` half, not the `offenders` half. That is the live regression risk now: collapsing the ladder back to two steps.
